title: Secure and Efficient Block-Cipher Key Schedules
summary: Numerous block-cipher key-schedule candidates have been broken in related-key or hash-function settings; a secure, efficient design resistant in both remains open.

formal_statement.body: For block ciphers, determine how to construct a key schedule that is both secure and efficient and resists attacks in the related-key model and attacks arising in a hash-function setting. This question remains open despite the symmetric-key cryptography community's good experience constructing secure and efficient fixed permutations, and numerous block-cipher key-schedule candidates have been broken in the related-key model or in a hash-function setting.

scope.domain: Design and cryptanalysis of block-cipher key schedules.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct a secure and efficient block-cipher key schedule that resists related-key attacks and attacks arising in a hash-function setting.

citations.label: Structural Evaluation of AES and Chosen-Key Distinguisher of 9-Round AES-128

progress.summary: The paper explicitly identifies block-cipher key-schedule design as an open problem. It contrasts this with experience building secure, efficient fixed permutations and notes numerous candidates broken in related-key or hash-function settings.
